It is singular in three MSS., and in all the early Versions, and the Targum; and the verb which follows requires it to be so, —
40. And I will bring on you a perpetual reproach, And a perpetual shame, which shall not be forgotten.
The word for “shame” is stronger than that for “reproach,” as Parkhurst tells us; but shame is the feeling, and is rendered sometimes confusion, and reproach is what is outwardly disgraceful. The Sept. and Vulg. have reproach and disgrace, by which the distinction is not marked. The reproach or disgrace was to be such as to create such a shame as would never be forgotten. The outward reproach is mentioned first, and then the shame that it would occasion. — Ed
et postea addit verbum singulare, oblivioni non tradetur; sed potest, quemadmodum dixi, hoc extendi ad totum complexum.
entries.bde437fb060b22630d601f95df9f32dd6adb66e1:
What is here contained is, that though the Jews justly gloried for a time in being the peculiar people of God, yet this would avail them nothing, as they had divested themselves of that honor in which they had excelled, by the abnegation of true religion. Here then the Prophet strips the Jews of that foolish boasting with which they were inflated when they said that they were the people of God, and threatens that God having taken away their glory would make them lie under perpetual shame.
We at the same time know, that such threatenings are to be restricted as to time, they extend only to the coming of Christ; for the Church of God could not have been doomed to eternal reproach. But as to hypocrites, as there was no repentance, so they never obtained pardon; but God delivered his own from eternal reproach when Christ the Redeemer appeared; yet these words are to be understood as rightly addressed to the ungodly despisers of God. Now follows, —
CHAPTER 24
Jeremiah 24:1-2
1. The LORD shewed me, and, behold, two baskets of figs were set before the temple of the LORD, after that Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon had carried away captive Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah, and the princes of Judah, with the carpenters and smiths, from Jerusalem, and had brought them to Babylon.
1. Videre me fecit (ostendit mihi visionem) Jehova, et ecce duo calathi ficuum positi coram Templo Jehovae, postquam transtulerat Nebuchadne-zer, rex Babylonis, Jechoniam, filium Joakim, regem Jehudah, et principes Jehudah, et artificem et inclusorem (vel, sculptorem)
What this word exactly means it is difficult to know; it is rendered differently in the Versions and in the Targ. It is rendered here by the Sept. “prisoners,” and in 2 Kings 24:14 and 16, “encloser, or joiner — συγκλείς;” by the Vulg. in three places, “clausor,” and “inclusor — closer and incloser,” and also in Jeremiah 29:2. The word is not found elsewhere. The Targ. renders it “porters,” and the Syr. “soldiers.” As the word “artificer,” or mechanic, includes workers in wood and iron, that is, carpenters and smiths, it is probable that מסגר means workers in embroidery, sculpture, and jewellery, Parkhurst was disposed to render it a setter, or incloser of precious stones; but Blayney renders it an armourer, who made the coats of mail which inclosed the body, as the word from which it comes means to inclose. It probably includes all engaged in the curious works of art, especially the three branches before mentioned. Perhaps the best modern word for it would be, the artist, —
“after Nebuchadrezar, the king of Babylon, removed Jeconiah, the son of Jehoiakim, the king of Judah, and the princes of Judah, and the mechanic and the artist, from Jerusalem, and brought them to Babylon.”
— Ed.
e Jerusalem, et ab-duxerat eos Babylonem:
2. One basket had very good figs, even like the figs that are first ripe: and the other basket had very naughty figs, which could not be eaten, they were so bad.
2. Calathus unus ficuum bonarum valde, sicuti sunt ficus praecoces; et alter calathus ficuum malarum valde, quae non comederentur propter malitiam (hoc est, adeo malae erant.)

               <ns0:p n="2">2 Therefore thus saith the LORD God of Is<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rael against the pastors that feed my people <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">God calleth them <ns0:hi>his People, his Flock, the Sheep of his Pa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sture,</ns0:hi> with respect to the ancient Covenant which God had made with their Fathers, <ns0:hi>Abraham, Isaac</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iacob,</ns0:hi> they are said to have fed this people, because it was their duty, and the busi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness of their office so to have done, though they had failed in it.</ns0:note>, Ye have scattered my flock, and driven them away, and have not visited them <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">And had done the quite contrary scattering them by their acts of <ns0:hi>Violence</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>oppression,</ns0:hi> and driving them from their places to seek some more safe, and quiet places of abode, or by their pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />digious wickednesses; having been the cause of their being carried into Captivity not visiting them, that is taking any due care of their good and welfare, seeing what they wanted, and supply<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing them, as good Rulers ought to have done.</ns0:note>; Behold, I will visit upon you the evil of your doings, saith the LORD <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">For which neglect God threatneth to visit upon them, the evil of their do<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ings, the <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> word signifieth to visit with a visitation of care and love, and also with a visitation of justice and severity, and is often so used in Holy Writ.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 And I will gather the remnant of my flock out of all countreys whither I have driven them <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">God puts a difference betwixt those that were misled by the examples of others, and the Rulers who set them such an ill ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ample, he threatned <ns0:hi>Iehojachim</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iehojakin</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Ieconiah,</ns0:hi> that they should return no more, but for the people, he here pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />miseth them a return at least a remnant of them, when he should have punished <ns0:hi>the goats</ns0:hi> as he speaketh <ns0:hi>Zech.</ns0:hi> 10.3.</ns0:note>, and will bring them again to their folds <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">By their <ns0:hi>Folds,</ns0:hi> he meaneth <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> and other Cities the Towns of <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi> which they had formerly inhabited:</ns0:note>, and they shall be fruitful, and increase <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Where they should once more be in prosperity. He speaks here concerning the return of this people out of the Captivity of <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> though there be some that think this text is primarily to be understood, <ns0:hi>of the gathering together in one, the people of God scattered abroad,</ns0:hi> in and by Christ according to the prophesie of <ns0:hi>Caiaphas, Iohn</ns0:hi> 11.52.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 And I will set up <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 3.15. Ezek. 34.11. &c.</ns0:note> shepherds over them which shall feed them <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Some think this Prophesie was fulfilled in <ns0:hi>Nehemiah</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Zo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />robabel,</ns0:hi> who were pious and good Governours, and consulted in their Government the good of the people committed to their trust. <ns0:hi>Neh.</ns0:hi> 2.10. and 5.14. Others rather understand it of Christian Princes and Governours, under the Gospel.</ns0:note>, and they shall fear no more, nor be dismayed <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Under whom they shall live peaceably and securely.</ns0:note>, neither shall they be lacking saith the LORD <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">And none of them shall perish. The two last passages of this verse incline In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terpreters to think, that this promise doth not so much refer to their coming out of <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> as to their spiritual deliverance by Christ, for after their return out of <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi> they were not secure long, but feared <ns0:hi>Sanballat</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Tobiah,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Grecians</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Romans</ns0:hi> and other Enemies, besides that the last words exactly agree with, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 10.28. when Christ saith his Sheep should not <ns0:hi>perish,</ns0:hi> and it appears verse 6. that the Prophet is speaking of a time, when not <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi> onely, but <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> also should be saved, and the next verse doth manifestly refer unto Christ.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 ¶ Behold, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Isa. 11.1. & 40.11. chap. 33.14, 15. Dan. 9.24. Joh. 1.45.</ns0:note> the dayes come, saith the LORD, that I will raise unto David, a righte<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ous branch <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Though some Interpreters think that <ns0:hi>Zorobabel</ns0:hi> may be here intended, who was descended from <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> and ruled the peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple when they came out of <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> yet, even the Jewish <ns0:hi>Doctors</ns0:hi> themselves, as well as the Christian Interpreters, understand this as a Prophesie, and promise of the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi>; the Prophesies and Promises of whom are usually ushered in with this par<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>icle <ns0:hi>Behold,</ns0:hi> to stir up peoples attention, and who also was the <ns0:hi>Son of David,</ns0:hi> and who is called <ns0:hi>the branch, Isa.</ns0:hi> 4.2. and 53.2. <ns0:hi>Zech.</ns0:hi> 3.8. and 6.12. where the reason is also given, he being there called <ns0:hi>a rod out of the stem of Iesse, a branch out of his root,</ns0:hi> besides that the application to him of the name <ns0:hi>King,</ns0:hi> ordinari<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly applyed to Christ, never given to <ns0:hi>Zorobabel,</ns0:hi> and the term <ns0:hi>Righteous</ns0:hi> make it evident, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 33.15. he is called a <ns0:hi>
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> of Righteousness,</ns0:hi> which is the same with the <ns0:hi>Righteous Branch,</ns0:hi> here mentioned, he is called the <ns0:hi>Righteous <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>,</ns0:hi> not only because himself was <ns0:hi>Righteous,</ns0:hi> therefore called the Righteous One, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 3.14. and 13.35. but because he maketh his people <ns0:hi>Righteous, Isa.</ns0:hi> 53.11. and 60.21.</ns0:note>, and a king shall reign, and pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sper, and shall execute justice, and judgment in the earth <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Jesus Christ answering the Type of <ns0:hi>Melchisedeck</ns0:hi> the King of <ns0:hi>Salem</ns0:hi> and who is <ns0:hi>the King of Kings,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 6.15. <ns0:hi>shall reign</ns0:hi> spiritually and shall not be like <ns0:hi>Ieco<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />niah</ns0:hi> of whom God said he should not prosper, but he shall pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sper and shall execute <ns0:hi>justice</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>judgment,</ns0:hi> protecting the inno<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cent, and defending his people throughout the World, judging the Prince of the World, and by his Spirit governing his people so as the Prophet relieveth the people of God under their op<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pressions, by these latter <ns0:hi>Kings of Iudah,</ns0:hi> with the promise of the Kingdom of Christ, an usual argument made use of by the Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets to comfort the people of God in those dayes against any evils come, or coming upon them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 33.28.</ns0:note> In his dayes Judah shall be <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 33.28.</ns0:note> saved, and Israel shall dwell safely <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">During the Reign & Kingdom of the <ns0:hi>Messias</ns0:hi> (whose Kingdom is an everlasting Kingdom) the people of God Typified by <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> the true <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> of God, those that are Jews indeed, shall be saved with a spiritual Salvation, for he was therefore called <ns0:hi>Iesus</ns0:hi> because he was <ns0:hi>to save his people from their sins, Matth.</ns0:hi> 1.21. and God will be a special protection to them.</ns0:note>: and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 33.16.</ns0:note> this <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> his name whereby he shall be called <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>Iehova<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                        <ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tsidkenu.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">The name wherewith this <ns0:hi>branch</ns0:hi> shall be called, shall be <ns0:hi>The Lord our Righte<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ousness.</ns0:hi> Some have applied this to the people as if the peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple should be so called, or should say the Lord hath dealt gra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ciously with us: or in the Lord we have Righteousness. But this will appear but the new invention of some who either can<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />not, or will not understand, how Christ should be his peoples Righteousness, to those who consider, that it is the <ns0:hi>branch</ns0:hi> which was before spoken of, and that the word <ns0:hi>people</ns0:hi> is not to be found going before, there is indeed a mention of <ns0:hi>Judah</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> but surely they were not to be other mens Righteousness, and if that had been the Prophets meaning he would not have said the Lord <ns0:hi>Our,</ns0:hi> but the Lord <ns0:hi>Their Righteousness.</ns0:hi> Nor is this the only place where Christ is called <ns0:hi>Our Righteousness,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 1.30. This place is an eminent proof of the Godhead of Christ, he is here called <ns0:hi>Jehovah,</ns0:hi> and what is proper to God alone, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>justifie</ns0:hi> is here applyed to Christ. The Prophet saith Christ shall be so called, that is by his people, who should believe in him and trust in him alone for that Righteousness, wherein they should at the last day stand before God, thus he was to bring in <ns0:hi>Ever<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lasting Righteousness, Dan.</ns0:hi> 9.24. <ns0:hi>He who knew no sin was m<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>de sin</ns0:hi> (that is a Sacrifice for sin) <ns0:hi>for us, that we might be made, the Righteousness of God in him.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 Therefore behold, the dayes come, saith the LORD, that they shall no more say, The LORD liveth, which brought up the children of Israel out of Egypt.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 But the LORD liveth, which brought up, and which led the seed of the house of Israel out of the north-country, and from all countreys whither I had driven them, and they shall dwell in their own land <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">See the Notes on <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 16.14, 15. Where much the same words are to be found. The Prophet aggravateth the greatness of that Salvation, which should be brought by Christ to all the true <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> of God, by comparing it with the deliverance of the ancient <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> of God out of the Land of <ns0:hi>Egypt</ns0:hi>; which he saith it should so far transcend and excel, that the deliverance out of <ns0:hi>Egypt</ns0:hi> should not be named, when this Salvation should appear, which should be after their return from <ns0:hi>Babylon,</ns0:hi> and when God should gather them from all Countries which was fulfilled, when by the Preaching of the Gospel, not the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> onely were Converted, but many of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> also which were scattered a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />broad, <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> 1.1. 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.1. Possibly part of this promise or prophesie remains yet to be accomplished, for the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> are not yet come to dwell in <ns0:hi>their own land,</ns0:hi> unless that term be to be expounded of Christians, who during the times of Persecution in the primitive Church, were scattered abroad, but upon the ceasing of those Persecutions, when Christian Emperours came to have the Government, returned to their own Countries, where they enjoyed a more still and quiet Habitation.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:32" />9 ¶ Mine heart within me is broken, because of the prophets, all my bones shake <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">The Prophet having denounced the Wrath of God against the wicked Rulers of <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi> under the Notion of <ns0:hi>Pastors,</ns0:hi> com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth here to discharge the like trust with reference to those or<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ders of Persons amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> whose office it was, or at least who took upon them to Reveal the Mind and Will of God to people, and who were upon that account called Prophets, for these he declares a great passion and trouble; either for their sake in prospect of that Vengeance of God which he saw was like to be poured out upon them, or for the Peoples sake who had been deceived by their unfaithful Revelations of the Divine Will, and led into wickedness by their vile Examples. For this he saith his heart was broken, his bones shaked.</ns0:note>: I am like a drunken man, and like a man whom wine hath overcome; because of the LORD <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">And he was even astonished and stupified, and like a drunken man he knew not what he did; he was so stricken at the apprehen<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sions of the Wrath of the Lord ready to be revealed against them.</ns0:note>, and because of the words of his holiness <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">And to consider what words the holy God had put into his mouth, to speak against them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 5.7, 8. & 9.2.</ns0:note> the land is full of Adulterers <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Under that term <ns0:hi>Adulterers,</ns0:hi> all Species of uncleanness are comprehended.</ns0:note>, for because of <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>cursing.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> swearing the land mourneth <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">By false-swearing, or by idle and profane swearing, the land is brought to ruine, the word signifies also a Curse or cursing, many good Interpreters judge, that the more genuine sense and true Translation of this Text were for <ns0:hi>because of the curse</ns0:hi> (that is, the Curse of God) the Land is brought to that Misery which is coming upon it.</ns0:note>: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 9.10. & 12.4.</ns0:note> the pleasant places of the wilderness are dried up <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">The pastures of the Wilderness or <ns0:hi>of the plain,</ns0:hi> for so the word is rendred, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 63.13. <ns0:hi>Lam.</ns0:hi> 4.19. The Wrath of God was extended to all places whether more or less inhabited.</ns0:note>, and their <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>violence.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> course is evil, and their force <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> not right <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">The Prophets did not onely err in single Acts, but the whole course of their actions was naught, and particularly their Power, Rule and Government was not right. If any say what were the Prophets concerned in the Peoples wickedness? <ns0:hi>Answ.</ns0:hi> They were profane as well as the people, as we shall find <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 11. but besides this, the people were thus vile through their connivance, they did not warn the people of their sins, but soothed them up in their wic<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ked courses, so were the cause of the peoples wickedness, who had not been so vile but for them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 For both <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 6.13. & 8.10. Zeph. 3.4.</ns0:note> prophet <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Those, whose work was to reveal the mind of God to the people, and who pretended to that office.</ns0:note> and priest are pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fane <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">And those that were employed in offering Sacrifices, and other works which belonged to the Priestly Office, according to the Law. The whole Ecclesiastical Order, all their Ministry were <ns0:hi>profane,</ns0:hi> not meerly hypocritical, but leud, immoral and debauched.</ns0:note>, yea, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 11.15. Ezek. 8.11. & 23.39.</ns0:note> in my house have I found their wickedness <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Yea, they were grown to that impudence that they made the Tem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple, which was the Lords house, a Den of Theeves; a place where they committed wickedness; thus it was in the time of <ns0:hi>Ely,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 2.22. and more generally afterward, 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 36.14. See <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 7.10, 11. & <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 14. of this <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> There is no more certain sign of a ruining Nation, than when God suffereth in it a leud and corrupt Ministry.</ns0:note>, saith the LORD.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 Wherefore <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 35.6. chap. 13.16.</ns0:note> their way shall be unto them, as slippery <ns0:hi>wayes</ns0:hi> in the darkness: they shall be driven on and fall therein <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">As their ordinary course is wicked and sinful, so they shall find that it will in the event be to them pernicious, perillous and full of danger, as a slippery path is to them that walk in a dark night, they shall be driven on till they fall therein. Courses of Sin may look smooth, but they alwayes prove slippery.</ns0:note>: for I will bring evil upon them, <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> the year of their visi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tation, saith the LORD <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">For I am resolved to punish their wicked courses; and to vi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sit them with my judgments.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 And I have seen <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>an absurd thing.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>unsavoury</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> folly in theprophets of Samaria <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">There was a time, when I saw folly in the Prophets that belonged to the ten Tribes, whose chief City was <ns0:hi>Samaria,</ns0:hi> the word translated <ns0:hi>folly</ns0:hi> signifies <ns0:hi>unsavoury,</ns0:hi> or an absurd thing. Our Saviour compareth wicked Ministers to <ns0:hi>unsavoury Salt, Matth.</ns0:hi> 5.13. Salt that is turned foolish (as the <ns0:hi>Gr.</ns0:hi> word signifies.) The Ministers of Gods word are, or ought to be, the <ns0:hi>Salt</ns0:hi> of the Earth, to season people with sound Doctrine, and by the good Example of an Holy Life, if they be corrupt in Doctrine or Manners, they become <ns0:hi>unsavoury,</ns0:hi> and the very worst of men. Such God sayes the Prophets of the ten Tribes were, before they were carried away Captive.</ns0:note>; they prophesied in Baal, and caus<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed my people Israel to err <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">They prophesied, pretend<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing they had their Instructions and Revelations from <ns0:hi>Baal,</ns0:hi> and so caused the ten Tribes to erre, which after the division of the Kingdom in <ns0:hi>Ieroboams</ns0:hi> time were called <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> in contra-di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stinction to the two Tribes and an half cleaving to the House of <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> which were called <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi> after the name of their princi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pal Tribe.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 I have seen also in the prophets of Jerusa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lem <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>filthiness.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> an horrible thing <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">The word signifies <ns0:hi>filthiness, stench,</ns0:hi> or an abominable thing, things every whit as bad, in some kind worse than what I saw in the Prophets of the 10 Tribes.</ns0:note>: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 29.23.</ns0:note> they commit adul<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tery <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">They commit not Spiri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tual Adultery onely, but Carnal Adultery, they are Whore<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mongers.</ns0:note>, and walk in lies <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">And they make it their business to instill falshoods into people, and entitle me to them, and this is their trade; not a single act, but their ordinary practice.</ns0:note>: they strengthen also the hands of evil doers, that none doth return from his wickedness <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">This is the great aggravation of the sin of those that occupy the place of Spiritual Guides, that they encourage profane men, either by their false Doctrine extenuating sin, and putting a fair gloss up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on them, or at least by their mealy Mouths fearing or forbear<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing to tell Sinners of their wicked Courses; or by their wicked Examples the most of people thinking they may do what their Teachers do, by which means Sinners instead of being brought to a sense of their sins and a repentance for them, are harden<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed in their wicked Courses.</ns0:note>, they are all of them unto me <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 3<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.32<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  </ns0:note> as Sodom, and the inhabitants thereof as Gomorrha <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">By this means <ns0:hi>all of them,</ns0:hi> either of their Prophets and Priests, or all of the People, (the first seemeth chiefly here intended) are become to me as contemptible, and abominable as the people of <ns0:hi>Sodom</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Gomorrah,</ns0:hi> though they were the Sons of <ns0:hi>Aaron,</ns0:hi> and of the Priestly Order, yet living leud lives, and acting quite contrary to the end of their Holy Calling, God declares himself to value them no more than as the vilest of men, such were the <ns0:hi>Sodomites.</ns0:hi> Or by those words God threatens that he would destroy them with as notorious a destruction, as he destroyed <ns0:hi>Sodom</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Gomorrha.</ns0:hi> Thus the comparison is used <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 1.9. and consonant to this are the words in the next verse.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 Therefore thus saith the LORD of hosts concerning the prophets <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Under the term Prophets he comprehendeth all the Eccle<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />siastical Guides of <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> at this time, whether <ns0:hi>Priests</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, Behold, I will feed them <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 8.14. & 9.15.</ns0:note> with wormwood <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">He threatens to feed them <ns0:hi>with wormwood,</ns0:hi> some think the word is better translated Poyson, by <ns0:hi>Wormwood,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>poyson</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>water of gall,</ns0:hi> he threatens great and fatal Judgments that he would bring upon them.</ns0:note>, and make them drink the water of gall: for from the prophets of Je<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rusalem is <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>Hypocrisie.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> profaneness gone forth into all the land <ns0:note n="a" place="margin">And he giveth the reason why God would deal so severely with that order of men, who seem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed by their office, and imployment to have the nearest Relati<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on to himself, because they were the Fountain of wickedness, those from whom wickedness flowed out over the whole land. This was either by their conniving at wicked mens sins, for fear of displeasing them; or by teaching them Licentious Do<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ctrine, that gave a liberty to the Flesh; or by their vile lives setting the people patterns of sin: And indeed thus it is gene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rally, when Ministers, and such as are to teach others, are wicked, either in their Doctrine or Practice, they are a foun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tain of Wickedness; Wickedness floweth from them to the whole City, Town, Parish where they are imployed: And on the contrary it is observed that where God gives a Place a good Ministry, Goodness in one Degree or other floweth from them to the whole <ns0:hi>City, Town</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Parish.</ns0:hi> Though all are not Con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />verted, yet the generality are Civilized and Restrained from those gross and brutish immoralities which other places abound with. Ill Ministers must look for the severest indignation of God. Others sin, and shall die in their sins; but they teach o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers to break Gods Commandments, and have the sins of many to answer for, who perish either by their flatteries, or loose Doctrine, or looser Lives and Examples.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 Thus saith the LORD of hosts, Hearken not unto the words of the prophets, that pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phesie unto you <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">People are under no Religious Obligation to hear any thing but the Revealed Will of God, and are not to obey those that call to them for what that doth not call to them.</ns0:note>, they make you vain <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Nor to listen to them, the Scope of whose teaching is but to make them vain, sinfully vain; or to deceive their Souls, no Man is under an O<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ligation to deceive himself.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 14.14<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  </ns0:note> they
<ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:33" />
speak a vision of their own heart, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> not out of the mouth of the LORD <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">They pretend to Visions, that God hath revealed his Mind to them, in the same way as he useth to reveal himself to true Prophets; but there is no such thing; it is but a fiction of their own; Our Lord, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 7.15. gives us the same way to know <ns0:hi>false Prophets, ver.</ns0:hi> 20. <ns0:hi>By their fruits you shall know them.</ns0:hi> Let their external Mission be what, and which way it will, if what they teach agree not with the revea<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ed Will of God, they are false Prophets. Many of these Priests were regularly enough descended, and the Prophets regularly enough educated and constituted, yet by this shewed themselves false <ns0:hi>Prophets,</ns0:hi> that what they published was not from God, nor agreed with his revealed Will; therefore the people were under no Religious Obligation to hearken to them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 They say still unto them that despise me, The LORD hath said, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 6.14. & 8.11. Ezek. 13.10. Zech. 10.2.</ns0:note> Ye shall have peace <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Leud and corrupt Ministers, are an hatred and abomination in the house of the Lord, to all serious good People, and are therefore obliged to make themselves a Party of those that are like themselves, whose favour they cannot have without indul<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ging them in their Lusts. Hence they prophesie Peace to the vilest and worst of Men, who have no Patience of being daily alarum'd with hearing of the wrath of God due, and like to come upon them for their sins.</ns0:note>; and they say unto every one that walketh after the <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>stubborness.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> imagination of his own heart <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Hence they promise evil to those that walk according to the Counsels of their own heart, that is sinfully, for <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 6.5. <ns0:hi>Every imagination of the thoughts of mans heart, is onely evil, and that continually:</ns0:hi> Hence a sinful course is very often expressed in Scripture, under this Notion of walking after the Imaginations of our own heart; as <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 29.19. but it is most in prophesie; Vid. <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 3.17. & 7.24. & 9.14. & 13.10. & 16.12. & 18.12. Hence a Religious walking is called a <ns0:hi>Self-denying.</ns0:hi> None have a worse guide of their actions in their lapsed state, before Rege<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />neration, than their own hearts.</ns0:note>, No evil shall come upon you.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Job 15.8.</ns0:note> who hath stood in the <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>secret.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> counsel of the LORD, and hath perceived and heard his word? who hath marked his word, and heard <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Who besides us hath known the counsel of the Lord? ar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rogating to themselves a fellowship, and acquaintance with the Mind and Will of God. Or (which I should rather judge the ense) which of those Prophets, that Prophesie such terrible things against this City is a Privy Counsellor to God? The words seem rather to be the words of the false Prophets, either arrogating to themselves a peculiar acquaintance with God and Fellowship with him, from whence they knew his Mind, or mocking at <ns0:hi>Ieremy,</ns0:hi> and other true Prophets, as arrogating to themselves such a knowledge of the Mind and Counsels of God as indeed they had not, then (as some think) the words of <ns0:hi>Ieremiah</ns0:hi> denying them to have stood in Gods Counsels, or to have known his Mind and Will. This is all Ages hath been the practice of corrupt Prophets and Ministers to charge those Servants of God, who have faithfully published the Will of God against Sinners, as making too bold with Gods secret Counsels, though they publish nothing but Gods revealed Will.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 Behold, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 25.32.</ns0:note> a whirlwind of the LORD is gone forth in fury <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">A severe judgment of God<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> that should resemble a Whirl<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wind, for the sudden and utter destruction, that it shall bring. See <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 30.23, 24. The same word is elsewhere translated a storm, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 83.15. <ns0:hi>Amos</ns0:hi> 1.14. <ns0:hi>Ionah</ns0:hi> 1.4. It is called a whirlwind <ns0:hi>of the Lord</ns0:hi>; either to denote the greatness of it, as <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 36.6. or to let us know that the Judgment came forth from God and was of his sending.</ns0:note>, even a grievous whirl<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wind, it shall fall grievously upon the head of the wicked <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">And whatever these flattering Teachers said, it should fall upon wicked men, so as they should have no peace, but evil should most certainly come upon them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 The <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 30.24.</ns0:note> Anger of the LORD shall not return, until he have executed, and till he have performed the thoughts of his heart <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">It is therefore called a <ns0:hi>continuing whirlwind, chap.</ns0:hi> 30.23. The Prophet speaks of the judgment as of a Messenger, which coming from God, should not return till it had done its Errand and Executed what it came for, even whatever God had resolv<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed should effect. Men are ready to flatter themselves, that they shall either out-ride or out-live the stormes of Divine Venge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ance, no (saith the Prophet) the Anger of the Lord shall bring to pass whatsoever the just Will of God is.</ns0:note>: in the latter dayes ye shall consider it per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fectly <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">And though you will not now believe it, but flatter your selves with idle, vain hopes, yet hereafter when it shall be too late (which is the usu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />al folly of Sinners) then you shall consider it perfectly.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 14.14 & 27.15. & 23.9.</ns0:note> I have not sent these prophets, yet they ran: I have not spoken unto them, yet they prophesied.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 But if they had stood in my counsel, and had caused my people to hear my words <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">These false Prophets did not Prophesie without the Appro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bation of the Rule<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> of the Ecclesiastical state amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> in their corrupt estate, but so they might, and yet not be sent of God. The Judgment of a Divine Mission for the Revelation of Gods Mind unto people, must not be meerly from their Ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ternal Mission (which yet they ought to have in a Church that is in order) but from the faithful discharge of their Ministry. Those whom God sends, and who are truly acquainted with his Counsels, will cause his people to hear, not their own conceits, and inventions, but the Word of the Lord. God sendeth none upon any other errand, but to reveal his Will, and tell his Mind unto people.</ns0:note>, then they should have turned them from their evil way, and from the evil of their doings <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Then, saith the Prophet, <ns0:hi>they should have turned them from their evil way,</ns0:hi> that is, they would have made this their scope, business and end, to turn Sinners from their sinful wayes, and though possibly their labour would not have had so good an effect upon all, yet they would have had an ef<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fect upon some to turn them from their evil doings.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 <ns0:hi>Am</ns0:hi> I a God at hand, saith the LORD, and not a God afar off <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Atheisme is generally the foundation of ill Life, men say, God sees them not, the Almighty doth not regard them. By a <ns0:hi>God at hand</ns0:hi> many understand Heaven, do you think that my eyes are limited like yours, that I cannot see their practices though far off from me? that is from the place of my glorious Residence. Others interpret the particle with respect to time; Am I a God of Yesterday, like the Idols, am not I the ancient of dayes? the Eternal God whose Majesty and Omniscience, you ought to have taken notice of?</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 Can any <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 139.7. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> Amos 9.2.3.</ns0:note> hide himself in secret places that I shall not see him? saith the LORD: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 King. 8.2<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. Psal. 139.7.</ns0:note> do not I fill heaven and earth? saith the LORD <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">What do these Atheistical Priests, and Prophets, and Peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple think? do they think that I who am a God of purer eyes than to behold iniquity, see and take notice of what Doctrine they Preach, and what lives they live: if they did, surely they would not dare to do as they do. Do they think that I do not see, or take notice of them? Can any hide themselves out of my sight, I <ns0:hi>fill heaven and earth,</ns0:hi> not onely with my influ<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ence, but with my Essence; with the immensity of my Being; which as it cannot be circumscribed by the Air, so it is shut out of no place.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 I have heard what the prophets said that prophesie lies in my name, saying, I have dream<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed, I have dreamed <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Visions</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Dreames,</ns0:hi> were two usual wayes by which under the Law God made himself known of old to his Prophets, mak<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing them sometimes, being awake, to hear a voice; sometimes attended with, and proceeding upon, some visible appearance, sometimes not: at other times causing them, being asleep, to dream; and in their sleep revealing to them, as in a dream, what his will was they should declare and publish to his people. These false Prophets speaking what came into their own heads, and suted their own Lusts, or the Lusts of a debauched people to whom they spake; would pretend that God had revealed to them what they so published, in a dream; not in the mean time considering God took notice of these their little Arts, by which they cheated the people. But saith God, I am a God that know afar off, as well as at hand, and I have heard what they say, <ns0:hi>Prophesying</ns0:hi> lies as from me, and pretending that I had in dreams revealed them to them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 How long shall <ns0:hi>this</ns0:hi> be in the heart of the prophets that prophesies lies? yea, <ns0:hi>they are</ns0:hi> prophets of the deceits of their own heart <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Will these Prophets never have done? Have they not de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceived people long enough with their lyes, and the deceit of their own hearts? and that not unwarily, and by involuntary mistake, but of set purpose it being in their heart, their pur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pose and design to do it. Some join it to the following Verse, and make the sense this; Do these Prophets that publish lies, and the deceits of their hearts, for my revealed Will, think to cheat my people always, and to cause my people to forget my name? as it followeth in the next verse.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 Which think to cause my people to forget
<ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:33" />
my name <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">That is to forget me, and those things by which I have made my self known unto them, my Word, and my Works.</ns0:note> by their dreams which they tell eve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry man to his neighbour <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">By their <ns0:hi>Dreams</ns0:hi> which they tell abroad every one to his Neighbour, as if they were Revelations which I had in their sleep made unto them, but they are indeed lies, and nothing but the deceits of their own hearts.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Judg. 3.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. & 8.33, 34.</ns0:note> as their fathers have forgotten my name for Baal <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">So that in effect they are <ns0:hi>Baals Priests</ns0:hi>; for as <ns0:hi>Baals Prophets,</ns0:hi> by publishing their pretended Revelations from <ns0:hi>Baal,</ns0:hi> seduced the people from the service and obedience of the true God; so these by telling their pretended dreames, seduced men from their obedience to God in what he revealed to them by the true Prophets, they agreed in the end, the se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ducing of the people from God, though they differed in the mean, the one pretending Revelations from <ns0:hi>Baal,</ns0:hi> the other from the true God by their Dreams.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 The prophet that <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>with whom is.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> hath a dream <ns0:hi>w,</ns0:hi> let him tell a dream; and he that hath my word let him speak my word faithfully <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">And let him to whom I have revealed my Will, publish and declare that in all Truth and Faithful<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness, not adding his own fancies or dreams to it, 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 2.17. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 2.2. not corrupting my word.</ns0:note>: what <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the chaffe to the wheat? saith the LORD <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">There is as much difference between my Will, and their Dreams, as there is be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />twixt the <ns0:hi>chaffe and the wheat</ns0:hi>; the one is of value to make food for the Soul, as wheat doth for the Body; the other is of no value: the one (<ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> my Word) is of a solid, abiding sub<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stance, the other is light and airy, and easily scattered by every Wind.</ns0:note>.<ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Not a Divine Dream; a Revelation which I have made to him in his sleep: as appeareth by the following opposition, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />twixt a <ns0:hi>dream,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>the word of the Lord,</ns0:hi> but if any man hath dreamed an ordinary dream, let him tell it as a dream; let him not entitle God to it.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 <ns0:hi>Is</ns0:hi> not my word like a fire <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Full of life and efficacy, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 6.63. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 4.12. like a fire, that warmeth, and healeth, and melteth, and consumeth the dross.</ns0:note>? saith the LORD, and like an hammer <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> breaketh the rock in pieces <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">And like an hammer that breaketh the flints, so my Word breaketh hard hearts. Others think, that the Word is here compared to fire, and to an hammer, because of the certain effect that it should have upon those that would not o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bey it, to burn them up like fire, and break them in pieces like an hammer, and so think this Text well expounded by the Apostle, 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 2.16. Certain it is, that Gods word is like fire in both senses, no words of men have an effect and efficacy like Gods Words, nothing but that taketh hold upon the Consci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ence, and hath such an effect upon the hearts of men. No words shall so certainly and infallibly be justified and made good.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 Therefore behold, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 18.20. ch. 14.14, 15.</ns0:note> I <ns0:hi>am</ns0:hi> against the pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets, saith the LORD, that steal my words, e<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />very one from his neighbour <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">There are various opinions, as to what the Prophet mean<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth here by those Prophets that <ns0:hi>stole the Lords words</ns0:hi> from their Neighbours; Some, by their Neighbour, understanding the true Prophets, from whom they stole those forms of Speech, <ns0:hi>Thus saith the Lord,</ns0:hi> or, <ns0:hi>The word of the Lord,</ns0:hi> or, <ns0:hi>The burden of the Lord.</ns0:hi> Or some of the matter which they prophesied, though they mixed it with their own lies and deceits. Others by Neighbours understanding their associates, think that these false Prophets conspired together what to say to deceive the people, and so stole what they said one from another. Or, the generality of the People from whom they are said to steal the Lords Word, because they withheld it from them injuriously. Or by their Arts and Flatteries brought men out of love with, or fear of the Words of the Lord, which had by the true Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets been delivered to them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 Behold, I <ns0:hi>am</ns0:hi> against the prophets, saith the LORD, that <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>that smooth their tongues.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> use their tongues <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Some think the <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> word were more properly translated <ns0:hi>smooth their tongues:</ns0:hi> Vid. The <ns0:hi>English</ns0:hi> Annotations.</ns0:note>, and say, He saith <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">But the next words seem to assure us that the crime for which God here by the Prophet, reflecteth upon the false Prophets, was not so much their flattering People, and speaking to them such smooth things as pleased them, as their entitling of God to their lies, saying, <ns0:hi>He,</ns0:hi> that is, <ns0:hi>The Lord saith.</ns0:hi> So it may be, though the word might be translated <ns0:hi>smooth,</ns0:hi> yet it is here better translated <ns0:hi>use.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 Behold, I <ns0:hi>am</ns0:hi> against them that prophesie false dreams, <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">That is, false things under the notion of things which I have revealed unto them in their sleep.</ns0:note>, saith the LORD, and do tell them, and cause my people to erre by their lies, and by their <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Zeph. 3.4.</ns0:note> lightness <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">By lightness, here some understand volubility, and smoothness of tongue and speech: Others, lasciviousness: Others levity and inconstancy, the last seemeth most probably the sense.</ns0:note>, yet I sent them not, nor commanded them: therefore they shall not profit this people at all, saith the LORD <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">I sent them not (saith God) therefore they shall not profit, none can expect Gods blessing upon their Ministry, that are not called, and sent of God into the Ministry.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 ¶ And when this people, or the prophet, or a priest shall ask thee, saying, What <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the burden of the LORD <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">The true Prophets to let the People know how l<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ttle plea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sing it was to them to be the Messengers of Gods threatnings, to denounce his judgments, usually began their prophesies of that nature calling them, <ns0:hi>The burden of the Lord,</ns0:hi> as may be seen, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 13.1. & 15.1. & 22.1. <ns0:hi>Hab.</ns0:hi> 1.1. <ns0:hi>Zech.</ns0:hi> 9.1. <ns0:hi>Mal.</ns0:hi> 1.1. The profane People and false Prophets, and corrupt Priests, not lov<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing to hear their doom, would ordinarily mock at the true Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets; and in derision ask them, what <ns0:hi>was the burden of the Lord?</ns0:hi> what ill news they had for them next?</ns0:note>? thou shalt then say unto them, What burden? I will even forsake you, saith the LORD <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">God bids the Prophet tell them, That God would forsake them, either as to the Spirit of prophesie, they should have no more Prophets or (which is more probable) as to his special Providence, by which he had watched over, protected, and hitherto defended them; a <ns0:hi>Bur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />den</ns0:hi> heavy enough, <ns0:hi>Hos.</ns0:hi> 9.12.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 And <ns0:hi>as for</ns0:hi> the prophet, and the priest, and the people that shall say, The burden of the LORD <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">That is, That shall in derision say thus, mocking at my threatnings and Judgments.</ns0:note>, I will even <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>visit upon</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> punish that man and his house <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">I will not only punish him but his whole Family.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">Thus shall ye say every one to his neigh<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bour, and every one to his brother, What hath the LORD answered? and, What hath the LORD spoken <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">I will have you speak more reverently of me and my Word to my Prophets.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 And the burden of the LORD shall ye men<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion no more <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">Not in scorn and derision, as not believing there were any such judgments, as they threaten, nor <ns0:hi>hardly</ns0:hi> as if I sent you no other messages but burdens.</ns0:note>: for every mans word shall be his burden <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">These false and irreverent speeches which are in every mans mouth, shall be burdensom to them, being such, as shall bring down divine Vengeance upon them.</ns0:note>: for ye have perverted the words of the living God <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Because you have derided, or misinterpreted the words of God, the living God.</ns0:note>, of the LORD of hosts our God <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">The sin of which is the more aggra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vated against you, because he is the living, mighty God, and because he hath been our God.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 Thus shalt thou say to the prophet <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">To my true Prophet. You shall speak to them reverent<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly, and as becometh you.</ns0:note>, What hath the LORD answered thee? and what hath the LORD spoken.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 But sith ye say, The burden of the LORD; therefore thus saith the LORD, Because you say this word, The burden of the LORD <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Because you go on in your scoffing, and deriding my Word and my Prophets.</ns0:note>, and I have sent unto you, saying, ye shall not say, The burden of the LORD <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">And that when I have expresly forbidden you those profane speeches, or that deriding form of speech; adding further contempt to your former profaneness.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 Therefore behold, I, even I will utterly forget you <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">I will forget you as to my Affection, and that is more than if all your friends forgat you. There is a great Emphasis in the doubling of the Pronoun, <ns0:hi>I even I.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, and I will forsake you <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">I will forsake you as to the presence of my special gracious Providence.</ns0:note>, and the city that I gave you and your fathers <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">And do not flatter your selves that I will not do it, because of your fathers, or because I gave this City to your fathers, for that very City I will withdraw my special Providence from, and that land, which heretofore was called, <ns0:hi>The land which the Lord thy God careth for<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> upon which the eyes of the Lord are alwayes from the beginning of the year, even to the end of the year, Deut.</ns0:hi> 11.12.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>and cast you</ns0:hi> out of my presence <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">And I will cast both City, and people out of my gracious Presence. So as I will no longer do them good as I have done.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="40">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:34" />40 And I will bring an everlasting reproach upon you <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">And you shall be a reproach, and that not for a few dayes but for ever.</ns0:note>, and a perpetual shame which shall not be forgotten <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">And a penal shame, which neither you nor those that see or hear of it shall forget. See such expressions, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 20.11.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
